rows.theme: Outward confession of belief contrasted with private allegiance and mockery

candidate_sources.relationship: related theme: external profession vs internal disposition
candidate_sources.shared: Contrast between outward religious words and inward disloyalty or disbelief.
candidate_sources.differences: Isaiah contrasts lip-honor of God with a distant heart and instruction by human rule; Qur'an 2:14 reports a group professing belief before believers and privately expressing allegiance and mockery. Settings and claims differ.

rows.theme: Deafness, speechlessness, blindness as moral-spiritual imagery

candidate_sources.relationship: related theme: spiritual inability to hear and see
candidate_sources.shared: Impaired hearing and seeing are used as metaphors of an unresponsive spiritual condition.
candidate_sources.differences: Isaiah features a prophetic commission addressed to a particular people, while Qur'an 2:18 characterizes the subjects of a preceding parable as deaf, mute, and blind; the imagery and rhetorical contexts are not identical.
